text: The 'common kind assumption', which disjunctivism rejects, states that:
choices: A veridical perception and a subjectively indistinguishable hallucination are experiences of the same fundamental kind
All perception is of mind-independent physical objects
Hallucinations have no phenomenal character at all
explanation: The common kind assumption says a veridical perception and an indistinguishable hallucination are experiences of the same fundamental kind; the argument from hallucination relies on it, and disjunctivism (McDowell, Hinton) rejects it. Options 1-3 are unrelated theses - direct realism, a category error about sense-data, and a denial of hallucinatory phenomenology.
